evidence_frontier: Widths 8, 10, and 12 have each passed the 100‑epoch local‑width confirmation gate (candidate_correct ≥ control_correct‑10) on ECG200 using fresh seed sets. The 50‑epoch w8 trial failed, but the 100‑epoch w8 trial succeeded, establishing that the gate can be met at multiple widths under the standard protocol.
analysis: Observations: (1) Candidate widths 8, 10, and 12 all achieved aggregate Q.ANT correct counts within 10 of their w16 controls after 100 epochs on fresh seeds. (2) The aggregate correct counts for candidates are 444 (w8), 444 (w10), and 445 (w12) versus controls 448, 453, and 453 respectively. Hypothesis: If the gate holds for intermediate widths, it may also hold for a wider local width such as 14, indicating that performance robustness extends to larger widths under the same training regime.
hypothesis: A local width of 14 will satisfy the preregistered gate (candidate_correct ≥ w16_control_correct - 10) when evaluated under the standard 100‑epoch ECG200 protocol, demonstrating that the gate’s validity persists for wider configurations.

proposal.title: 100‑epoch Confirmation of Local Width 14 on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Does a local width of 14 meet the preregistered performance gate relative to the width‑16 control under the standard 100‑epoch ECG200 protocol?
proposal.rationale: Widths 8, 10, and 12 have each been shown to meet the gate, but the behavior of wider local widths remains untested. Confirming width 14 will extend the empirical understanding of the width‑response curve and assess whether the gate continues to hold as the model becomes less compressed.
proposal.risks: The candidate may fail the gate, providing a negative result that still informs the width‑response relationship. Additional risk includes potential over‑parameterization leading to diminishing returns, but the experiment remains low‑cost and bounded.
